Kimberly —

Thanks for the package and helpful breakdown. Quick answers inline: 

> Are the gating thresholds below appropriate for an alpha assessment (critical controls + top 10 high-risk control families), or should we expand to include the medium-risk control families?

For an alpha intake, keep to critical + top 10 high-risk families. Including medium controls will significantly increase sampling overhead; recommend we add them only for the full FedRAMP readiness run.

> Do you need us to provide both system-level snapshots and enclave-level configurations, or will system-level be sufficient for the first intake?

System-level snapshots are fine initially, *provided* you flag any enclave-specific deviations in the intake workbook. If you can include one enclave-level snapshot for a representative tenant, that will reduce follow-ups.

> Can the auditors accept our proposed sampling windows (US-west: Jan 18–22; US-east: Jan 25–29) or do they require a continuous 2-week window?

Those windows are acceptable. We prefer staggered windows to avoid resource conflicts. Auditors can do the dry-run over the two separate weeks.

I'll loop in our audit lead with the calendar invite after you confirm owners for the control families and the drive link.

Regards,
Daniel Park
Principal Auditor, NetGov Security
--
